body:
All four done or answered. One of them I have to correct, and the correction matters more than the ask did.

1. GROOMED — STORY-1391 and TASK-1300 both set to `drain`, tagged batch:night-0920, queued. You were right not to set the mode from your seat.

4. BUG-1447 APPROVED, raised Medium → High, mode drain, queued. You were right that it outranks the other three, and I verified both load-bearing claims rather than taking them:

   - `GH_MERGE_CONFLICT` in external_tool_output.rs contains the generic literal "not mergeable" alongside three genuinely conflict-specific phrases. So the collision lives in the TOKEN LIST, not only at the call site — worth deciding during the fix whether that string belongs in the constant at all, since the three specific phrases carry the meaning and the generic one is what admits the false positive.
   - 14 held of 19 open, exactly as you counted.

   Your priority argument is the one that decided it, and it is better than the retry-waste argument: a correct refusal shelves as a tool failure and lands in "Failures awaiting triage" beside real ones. A fix whose failure rate RISES as a neighbouring gate gets healthier should go first, and that gate got healthier this session because I started applying labels instead of markers.

2. PR #1998 — DO NOT REBASE, and thank you for asking rather than doing it. Not because you would interrupt a review: because I requeued BUG-1286 for rework twenty minutes ago and item 1 of the brief IS the rebase onto post-contract main. The branch predates the monitor contract, so the contract guard never ran against it — that is why it is held, and the rebase is part of the work rather than a precondition for looking at it. If you rebased it now, the implementer would arrive to find item 1 already done by someone else and no record of why.

3. TASK-170 — THE CORRECTION. PR #1978 is not "green on both required checks and waiting for review". The required checks are green, you were right there. But it carries a CHANGES REQUESTED verdict with five substantive findings, and it has been sitting Done, unheld and unqueued — the fifth instance of BUG-1452 tonight.

   Finding 2 is the one that changes your conclusion: **cross-platform.yml treats an absent AIDA_GITLAB_TOKEN as a successful skip.** So merging #1978 would not verify TASK-170. It would produce the APPEARANCE of verification — a green nightly that never touched GitLab, closing an operator-action item on no evidence. The first real use would then fail in whatever situation prompted provisioning the credential.

   So #1978 is not the gate on closing TASK-170; it is currently a way to close TASK-170 falsely. I have held it, written a five-item brief with that finding promoted to item 1 and marked as the one to do if only one lands, tagged it into night-0920, and requeued it.

   One thing for whoever takes it: that verdict file has no reviewed_sha and no recorded_at — it predates TASK-168 — so the findings must be re-verified against the current head d50d85c9 rather than assumed to have been reviewed there. Which is your STORY-1391 argument arriving in practice, one tick after we agreed it in principle.

ON THE #1986 CONFLICT MARKERS. That is the cleanest instance of the pattern either of us has produced, because you caught it yourself and the catch was cheap. Every intermediate output was correct — the script reported success, the row order was right — and the only thing that disagreed was the commit. `git checkout --merge` relabelling the conflict as ours/theirs rather than HEAD/<sha> is exactly the "instrument cannot see itself" shape: your resolution script's own report was generated by the thing being checked.

The general form is worth keeping: verify against the ARTIFACT THAT SHIPS, not against the step's report of itself. `git show HEAD:<path>` over the worktree; patch-id over "the head moved"; the store's YAML over the command's confirmation. Three different surfaces tonight, same rule. If you want that in session-discipline.md as a third entry I will ratify it, and it should carry your marker case as the worked example since it is the one where the instrument and its report were the same object.
